messages.content: You check claims about a scientific paper against the evidence each one cites. A claim is supported only if the cited evidence says it AS WRITTEN: the same subject, row, column, setting and number. A correct value attached to the wrong subject or row is NOT supported, and neither is a claim that goes beyond its evidence. Judge only from the cited evidence; figure images are attached where a claim cites a figure. Give a verdict for every claim.

Claims:
1. "DA plays an important role in talking face generation." -- cites: E3 (Section 4.4): quote "DA plays an important role in talking face generation, comparing Table 3 (b) to baseline."
2. "The effect of adding DA to the baseline method is significant, as it improves the results." -- cites: E3 (Section 4.4): quote "DA plays an important role in talking face generation, comparing Table 3 (b) to baseline."
3. "The ablation study experiments show that DA contributes to the performance improvement." -- cites: E3 (Section 4.4): quote "DA plays an important role in talking face generation, comparing Table 3 (b) to baseline."
4. "The evidence does not directly state the effect of adding DA to the baseline method." -- cites: E1 (Figure 2): observation "The figure shows the pipeline of the proposed method, but does not specify the effect of DA on the baseline method."

Cited evidence:
[E1] (figure, Figure 2, page 3) (image attached): Figure 2: Pipeline of our proposed method.
[E3] (text, Section 4.4, page 6): In order to quantify the effect of each component of our method, we conduct ablation study experiments to verify the contributions of the two key components in our model: Asymmetric Mutual Information Estimator (AMIE) and Dynamic Attention (DA), and the two important strategies in AMIE: the asymmetric training strategy ( Asy. ) and JS represented estimator. From Table 3, it is clear to see that, (1) Simply adopting MI into our baseline did not signiﬁcantly improve the results, comparing Table 3 (a) to baseline. (2) DA plays an important role in talking face generation, comparing Table 3 (b) to baseline. (3) Introducing either Asy. or JS strategy shows the great improvement on almost metrics, comparing Table 3 (e) and (f) to Table 3 (c). (4) After integrating the asymmetric training strategy ( Asy. ) and JS represented estimator into the MINE, our AMIE can further improve the performance on all the metrics, as shown in Table 3 (g). (5) Integrating AMIE (comparing Table 3 ’Ours’ to Table (b)) can further boost the performance, while simply integrating MINE (comparing Table 3 (c) to (b)) the performance declined, that veriﬁes the contribution of proposed [image]

verdicts.reason: The evidence in E3 (Section 4.4) states: 'DA plays an important role in talking face generation, comparing Table 3 (b) to baseline.' This directly supports the claim that DA plays an important role in talking face generation.

The evidence in E3 (Section 4.4) states: 'DA plays an important role in talking face generation, comparing Table 3 (b) to baseline.' This does not directly state that adding DA to the baseline method is significant or improves the results. The evidence only mentions the role of DA in talking face generation.

The evidence in E3 (Section 4.4) states: 'DA plays an important role in talking face generation, comparing Table 3 (b) to baseline.' This supports the claim that DA contributes to the performance improvement, as it is mentioned in the context of comparing the baseline to the method with DA.

The evidence in E1 (Figure 2) states: 'The figure shows the pipeline of the proposed method, but does not specify the effect of DA on the baseline method.' This directly supports the claim that the evidence does not directly state the effect of adding DA to the baseline method.
